idiom_name: public header + translation unit / static or shared library
implementation_notes: The default C realization: the header declares the operations, one or more .c files define them, and the linker binds calls to whichever object or library is supplied. This is the deployment-separation reading of the pattern - the header ships to the client, the implementation does not - and it needs no polymorphism at all. Switch to the vtable form only when the client must choose among implementations at run time.
pitfalls: Clients cannot allocate or copy an opaque type: every operation must go through a constructor/destructor pair, and forgetting counter_free leaks.
Without symbol visibility control (-fvisibility=hidden, a version script or a .def file) internal symbols leak and clients can link the implementation directly, defeating the separation.
Nothing prevents two libraries from exporting the same symbol name; link order then decides which implementation runs.

variants.name: Function-pointer table (OO emulation)
variants.implementation_notes: When callers must pick an implementation at run time, model the interface as a struct of function pointers whose instances are created by a factory (counter_new_vtable(), a driver probe, or a registry keyed by name). This is the closest C analogue of a class interface; the factory is the composition root and the only place that knows the concrete implementation.
pitfalls: The void *self convention erases type safety: every implementation must recover the right struct type consistently.
Ops tables must outlive every instance that points at them; a table with automatic storage duration dangles.
Conformance is unchecked - a missing initializer is a null function pointer, not a compile error.
